messages:
maya: Bringing up bridge-9b-multilang int4 canary on dedicated. Seeing quality regression on FR/ES translation outputs and OOMs when max_new_tokens > 128. Logs attached. Anyone seen language-specific degradation with folding quant?

sam: which quant backend? ggml or custom int4?

maya: ggml-int4 (our usual), compiled with kernel 3.1. Kernel mismatch warning in build log but ran anyway.

ethan: can you paste the inference config?

maya: ```
model: bridge-9b-multilang
quant: ggml-int4
max_new_tokens: 256
batch_size: 2
prefetch: true
kv_cache: enabled
kernel_hint: auto
``` 

leana: fwiw, earlier we saw FR drop with asymmetric quant on tokenizers that mix accented chars. Did you run the tokenization check?

maya: ran quick stats — tokenization entropy lower for fr/es vs en. Example: "bonjour" vs "bonjour!" changed token boundaries more often.

ops: infra-bot detected 3 oom events on host gpu-04 at 1719456820, triggering auto-evict.

infra-bot: deploy-notice: Canary deploy bridge-9b-multilang int4 -> 2 replicas. OOM threshold tripped, scaled down to 1.

sam: logs?

maya: ```
[2026-05-01 12:07:22] ERROR oom: alloc 1.2GB failed
[2026-05-01 12:07:22] TRACE kv_cache: current_slots=4096 free_slots=12
[2026-05-01 12:07:22] WARN kernel: fallback to generic mm for attention
``` 

ethan: two hypotheses: (1) tokenization causes longer effective seq lengths -> more kv usage, (2) ggml-int4 kernel fallback increases memory due to temp buffers.

leana: test: try max_new_tokens=128 and microbatching (batch_size=1) + kv_trim_policy=on-demand

maya: started a canary with max_new_tokens=128, batch_size=1, kv_trim=on-demand. also testing symmetric quant variant.

bench-bot: perf snapshot: int4-canary-1: p95 latency 230ms, p50 120ms, token-cost 0.0018
bench-bot: int4-canary-2 (128max): p95 190ms, p50 100ms, token-cost 0.0017

maya: early anecdotal — FR outputs improved with 128 cap, less hallucination on named entities.

ops: please capture memprof on next OOM; add env REDWOOD_MEMPROF=1

maya: added memprof and will roll another canary in 10m. thanks all :rocket:

leana: if quality still bad, try eval set: fr-news, es-chat, en-docs and run BLEU/BERTscore diffs between fp16 and int4.

maya: good call — kicking off eval job.

sam: ping me if you want me to bisect quant weight scales.

maya: will do. thanks!
